t: No appropriations in this title shall be available to enter into any new lease of real property if the estimated annual rental cost is more than $1,000,000, unless the Secretary submits a report which the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress approve within 30 days following the date on which the report is received.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a report-and-approval requirement before a federal leasing decision is a formal consultation process. However, the only actors are the Secretary and the congressional Appropriations Committees, all of whom are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public is consulted or given a right to object, so this is not participation.
fable.s: unless the Secretary submits a report which the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress approve within 30 days following the date on which the report is received

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary to submit a report to Congressional committees for approval. Congress and its committees are part of the federal government. The definition explicitly states that reports to or notifications of Congress are inside the federal government and do not constitute participation. There is no involvement of outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities in this decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: unless the Secretary submits a report which the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress approve within 30 days following the date on which the report is received.

opus.w: Before a large lease can be signed, the Secretary must send a report to the House and Senate Appropriations Committees and get their approval. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so this is coordination within the government, not outside participation. The report-and-approval step looks procedural, but it doesn't involve the public, states, experts or any other non-federal party.
opus.s: unless the Secretary submits a report which the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress approve within 30 days following the date on which the report is received
opus.b: The obvious misreading is to call this participation because the lease can't go ahead until a report is submitted and approved. That reading fails because only Congress's Appropriations Committees review and approve the report. They are inside the federal government, so nobody outside the government takes part in the decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary to submit a report to the Committees on Appropriations of Congress for approval. Since Congress and its committees are part of the federal government, this interaction is intra-governmental. The definition explicitly states that reports to or notifications of Congress are not participation because Congress is inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: unless the Secretary submits a report which the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress approve within 30 days following the date on which the report is received.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Secretary must submit a report to Congress, this involves an external check or coordination. However, Congress is explicitly defined as being INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, reporting to or seeking approval from congressional committees is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties.
